Understanding the Uttar Pradesh One District One Product (ODOP) Financing Assistance Scheme

The Uttar Pradesh One District One Product (ODOP) Financing Assistance Scheme, commonly referred to as the ODOP Margin Money Scheme, is designed to support individuals in establishing or expanding business units centered around their district's designated traditional craft, food item, or local industry. Launched by the Uttar Pradesh Government in September 2018, the program is managed through the Directorate of Industries, its ODOP Cell, and local District Industries Centres (DIC).

Scheme Structure and Financial Assistance

The initiative addresses a common hurdle for small artisans and first-time entrepreneurs: arranging initial capital before securing a bank loan. Under this scheme, financial support is delivered through a combination of a bank loan and government margin money.

  • Margin Money Support: For projects costing up to ₹25 lakh, the government provides 25% of the project cost, capped at ₹6.25 lakh. For larger projects, the maximum margin money support can reach up to ₹20 lakh.
  • Grant Conversion: The margin money is deposited directly into the beneficiary's bank account via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) and acts as an interest-free portion of the financing. If the unit operates successfully for two consecutive years without defaulting on the loan, this margin money is converted into a non-repayable grant.
  • Promoter Contribution: General category applicants are required to contribute 10% of the total project cost, while applicants belonging to SC, ST, OBC, minority, women, or divyang categories need to contribute 5%.

Eligibility Criteria

To qualify for financial support under the scheme, applicants must meet specific administrative requirements:

  • Age: Applicants must be at least 18 years old.
  • Sector Alignment: The proposed unit must deal directly with the officially identified ODOP product of the applicant's home district within the industry, service, or business sectors.
  • Default Status: The individual or unit must not be a defaulter of any nationalized bank, financial institution, or government body.
  • Exclusivity: Applicants must not have availed benefits from any other central or state self-employment scheme. Only one member per family can receive support under this program.

Application and Verification Process

The application process is entirely digital, managed through the official Directorate of Industries portal. Offline submissions are not accepted.

  1. Online Registration: Applicants register on the official portal and select the ODOP Financing Assistance Scheme.
  2. Scoring System: Instead of interviews, applications are evaluated using a 100-mark credit scorecard. Submissions scoring 50 marks or higher are forwarded to a bank branch for loan consideration.
  3. Bank Processing: Designated bank branches review the forwarded application and decide on sanctioning or rejecting the loan within one month.
  4. Training and Disbursement: Following a loan sanction, new beneficiaries typically undergo short-term entrepreneurship training before the bank disburses the initial loan installment and the government releases the margin money via DBT.

Verification and Official Contacts

Applicants experiencing difficulties with the online process can seek hand-holding support from the Deputy Commissioner (Industries) at their local District Industries and Enterprise Promotion Centre (DIC) or visit a nearby Jan Seva Kendra (CSC). Original announcements, scheme guidelines, and updates can be verified directly through the official Directorate of Industries, Uttar Pradesh portal.
